description:
Found while profiling the compiler (2026-10-20, warm compiles, all test and example modules).

The copy analysis's entry points take about 16% of the compiler's real work: Copies.nested/3 9.7%, enter_stmt/4 4.5%, live_around/4 1.9% (SatEx.Kernels: nested 89 of 485 ms). For every nested block (an if/cond/case arm, a loop or fn body), nested/3 walks the whole enclosing statement several times: arm?/2 (occurrences/2 plus a prewalk over arms/1), taken/2 (occurrences/2 again, then a prewalk that calls holds_arm?/2 on every node, which walks the arms again: quadratic in the statement), and reads_outside/2 (read_counts/1 of the whole statement and of the arm). enter_stmt/4 walks each statement with reads/1, and statements nested in a loop are walked again for each level.

Do: compute, once per statement (when enter_stmt/4 sets s.stmt), what nested/3 needs for each arm: whether the node is an arm, and the names the statement reads outside it as taken/2 defines it. Then nested/3 is a lookup. Keep the definitions of arm?, taken and reads_outside as the spec (unit tests compare old and new on generated statements). Consider memoising reads/1 per statement for enter_stmt/4.

Expected: most of the 16%, about 10-12% of compile time. Measure with the warm-compile harness of the method ticket.

Gate: byte-identical mix dump_c against an untouched main checkout (noise: DEFK_HEADER_HASH, the path-hashed defk:loop key in Defk.ReportTest.Gen.c); mix ci; PR per AGENTS.md. Smaller cuts seen in the same profile, not part of this ticket: the report hint search Facts.residual/5 (2.4%, 6% on SatEx; it runs for every kept check, check how Defk.Report uses the notes first) and caching atom ranks in the prover (Facts.counter/4, about 1%).

comments.text: Branch defk-o08.3/copies-arm-reads pushed, stacked on defk-o08.2's branch (merge that PR first). arm_reads/2: C byte-identical, -9.2% reductions / -9.6% time, now +17.6% of the work before step 1 (performance.md 6.39); mix ci green. PR not opened yet.

title: Copy analysis: compute each statement's arm reads once (Copies.nested/3 is quadratic)
